insights.topic: Verified purchase data vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's cryptographically verified receipts represent a structurally different targeting input than cookie-based inference — $4.6M+ in confirmed GMV across 96K+ receipts means the dataset is real and growing, not theoretical. For brands paying $5+ CPM to guess at purchase intent, a receipt-verified signal set commands a different conversation about price and precision.

Grocery and supermarkets account for 1,377 of the 5,082 receipts in the trailing 14-day window — the single largest category by count — with a $44.52 average basket, above the dining and gas categories. Brands in adjacent categories (CPG, household, health) should note that grocery is where verified purchase density is concentrating.

insights.topic: $100K weekly GMV ceiling — pace is real but plateaued
insights.insight: Seven-day GMV has approached $100K three times ($99,263; $99,116; $95,413) without breaking through, and currently sits at $87,203 — a recovery from a rolling-window rolloff, not a demand drop. The ceiling signals a user base that is active and consistent but not yet in a growth phase that would shift the addressable audience size argument for brand buyers.

insights.topic: Retailer concentration tells you who the users are
insights.insight: The top five brands by 14-day receipt count — Walmart (325), Costco and Kroger (tied at 149), Safeway (144), Publix (127) — are all mainstream mass and grocery chains. This is not an affluent niche panel; it is a middle-market, everyday-spend consumer set, which is directly relevant for CPG, household goods, and value-positioned brand strategies.

insights.topic: Brand list freeze broke — new retailer categories entering
insights.insight: After 40+ consecutive snapshots with no new brands crossing the visibility threshold, The UPS Store and 7-Eleven both appeared within a 48-hour window. Convenience and shipping-adjacent retail entering the verified receipt stream suggests the user base is expanding beyond a grocery-anchored core, which matters for brands in impulse, snack, and on-the-go categories.

insights.topic: Unknown category carries the highest basket size
insights.insight: The 'Unknown' category — 411 receipts, $50.80 average GMV — posts the highest per-receipt spend in the dataset, above grocery, department stores, and gas. Until those receipts are classified, they represent both a gap in category intelligence and a signal that higher-ticket purchase behavior exists in the verified pool beyond what the labeled categories show.
